*** THE DAY'S SHAPE: THE BOND ROUT UNWOUND, AND OIL TOOK OVER ***
This morning's edition led on the thirty-year gilt breaking 6% for the first time since 1998. By the
close it had gone back under:
  UK10Y-GB  5.3934%  hi 5.5098%  lo 5.3607%   (down ~11.6bp from the day's high)
  UK30Y-GB  5.9416%  hi 6.0289%  lo 5.9127%   *** BACK BELOW 6% ***
  US10Y     5.239%   hi 5.344%   lo 5.205%    chg -0.054 on prev 5.293%
  US30Y     5.608%   hi 5.693%   lo 5.577%    chg -0.031 on prev 5.639%
So the 6% print stands as an intraday high that did not hold. Said plainly in the brief: the morning
edition's lead is now a high-water mark, not a level. Trading Economics agrees on direction for both.

*** OIL IS THE STORY INSTEAD: BRENT +4.5% ON A THIRD US CARRIER ***
@LCO.1 (Dec'26) 102.45, +4.51%, prev 98.03, hi 103.05, lo 96.55 — read 20:19 BST.
@LCO.2 (Jan'27)  98.56, +3.65%, prev 95.09.
CNBC's own market report (cached EVE-MKT-CNBC-brent-jumps-third-carrier.txt, 19:29 BST) gives the
settle: "Brent crude... jumped 4.4% to close at $102.31 per barrel, while U.S. West Texas Intermediate
futures climbed 2.7% to settle at $92.87." Cause: the US is sending a THIRD aircraft carrier strike
group to the Middle East, with Marine Corps ships and up to 10,000 additional troops, expected by the
end of November. USS Theodore Roosevelt left San Diego Sunday; USS George H.W. Bush and USS George
Washington are already on station. Sourced by CNBC to US officials speaking to the Wall Street Journal.
TICKER DECISION: publish the live 102.45 / +4.51% from the quote endpoint (the ticker is a live feed),
with the 102.31 / +4.4% settle recorded here as corroboration. Both figures are CNBC's.
NOTE THE SECOND DAY OF THE ROLL: @LCO.1 is December, as it has been since this morning. Yesterday
evening it was November at 103.62. Today's 102.45 is NOT comparable to that 103.62 — the contract
changed overnight. On a like-for-like December basis the two-day move is 98.03 -> 102.45.

FX — A GENUINE DIVERGENCE WORTH RECORDING. The ECB daily reference rate now exists for today:
Frankfurter gives EUR/GBP 0.85373 dated 2026-10-01. CNBC's 20:29 read is 0.8515, about 22 pips lower.
That is a wider gap than this week's usual agreement to four decimals. The explanation is timing rather
than disagreement: the ECB fixes at about 16:00 CET (15:00 BST) and sterling went on weakening after
it, with cable falling to 1.3182 at the low and finishing at 1.3194, down 0.54%. Both figures are
therefore right for their own moment; the ticker carries the live one.
THE NOTABLE DIVERGENCE OF THE DAY: sterling fell 0.54% even as gilt yields came DOWN. Yesterday it
firmed while yields rose; today it fell while they fell. Neither day moved the way the textbook says,
which is worth not over-explaining.
